DO NOT EMAIL ME Unless you are a Ham Radio Supplier. I make videos, I am NOT technical support, unless you want to pay me vasts amount of money :-). Vierwege-Antennenschalter mit 500 Watt und ESP32-Twist!

Tech Minds
Tech Minds

Bestätigt
143.000 Abonnenten
Herunterladen
7992 Aufrufe vor 2 Wochen #TechMinds #SDR #HamRadio
7.992 Aufrufe • 13.08.2025 • #TechMinds #SDR #HamRadio
In diesem Video sehen wir uns einen 4-Wege-Fernantennenschalter an, der Reichweiten von 160 m bis 6 m unterstützt. Als Bonus entwerfe ich außerdem eine Web-Benutzeroberfläche auf einem ESP32-Modul, um daraus einen echten Fernantennenschalter zu machen.  …...mehr
...mehr
Weniger anzeigen
The video explores a 500-watt, four-way antenna switch. It demonstrates how to integrate an ESP32 microcontroller to enable remote control of the switch via a web interface, allowing users to select different antennas and customize their names.

@marceldaverveld

vor 2 Wochen
Matt, you can simply add an extra safety so that never more then one relay is activated. Doe not wire the 12 V to all center pins of the blue relays but link the unused contact of the first relay trough to the middle pin of the second relay and second unused contact to middle third and so one. That way it is impossible to activate more then one relay no matter what the software says.

@mikewillis1592

vor 2 Wochen
I did something similar with an arduino. Well worth doing. Saves using a manual switch. Instead of relays you can use a couple of transistors in a high side switch configuration, or modify the relay board to work with low side switching and use a ULN7003 or similar darlington array. I am doing just that with a 6 way switch and Arduino monitoring the radio band selection output.

You could add a bit of logic to make a 2:4 decoder or use part of a 74ls138 3:8 decoder. It takes a binary number in and enables just one pin. E.g give it 011 binary 3 and pin 3 only is active. Obviously you’d need a level shifter or a couple of transistors too. nice idea I have been thinking of doing something similar but probably linking it to home assistant.
